verses.zh: 「那时，耶和华吩咐我说：『你要凿出两块石版，和先前的一样，上山到我这里来，又要做一木柜。
verses.en: At that same time the Lord said to me, “Carve out for yourself two stone tablets like the first ones and come up the mountain to me; also make for yourself a wooden ark.[NOTE:1]
notes: Or “chest” (so NIV84, CEV); NLT “sacred chest”; TEV “wooden box.” This chest was made of acacia wood; it is later known as the ark of the covenant.
verses.commentary:
10:1 "the mountain" This refers to Mt. Horeb/Mt. Sinai.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HOREB

SPECIAL TOPIC: LOCATION OF MT. SINAI

▣ Moses is to prepare for his second encounter with YHWH:

- "cut out for yourself two tablets of stone" ‒ BDB 820, KB 949, Qal IMPERATIVE, cf. Exod. 34:1,4

- "come up to Me" ‒ BDB 748, KB 828, Qal IMPERATIVE

- "make an ark" ‒ BDB 793, KB 889, Qal PERFECT with waw, cf. Exod. 25:10

The Hittite Treaties also required two copies of the agreements. One was given to the lesser king to
read every year and the other placed in the temple of the greater king's god. See Introduction to the book, VII.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HITTITE (SUZERAIN) TREATIES

▣ "ark of wood for yourself" Exodus 37:1 says Bezalel made the Ark of the Covenant. Rashi says details
of the ark were not even given until Moses came down the second time from Mt. Sinai. Therefore, Moses must have
made a crude ark first and then later Bezalel made another more elaborate one (cf. Exod. 25:10-22). This first ark, made
quickly by Moses, held only the Ten Commandments (cf. 1 Kgs. 8:9). The later one contained: the Ten Commandments,
a sample of manna, and Aaron's rod that budded . For a good brief discussion see Roland de Vaux, Ancient Israel, vol. 2, pp. 292-303.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE ARK OF THE COVENANT

verses.zh: 你先前摔碎的那版，其上的字我要写在这版上；你要将这版放在柜中。』
verses.en: I will write on the tablets the same words[NOTE:1] that were on the first tablets you broke, and you must put them into the ark.”
notes: The same words. The care with which the replacement copy must be made underscores the importance of verbal precision in relaying the Lord’s commandments.
verses.commentary:
10:2 "I will write" YHWH wrote the law, verse 4 and Exod. 34:1. However, Exod. 34:27 speaks of Moses writing. Possibly
YHWH wrote the Ten Commandments, but Moses wrote the descriptive and declarative material, which explained and applied
it. It was not Moses' mentality nor his cultural influence, but God who originated the Law. God used cultural examples and
forms that Moses would have been familiar with. In many ways the form of the Law is similar to Babylonian law, but the
content is different.

SPECIAL TOPIC: MOSES' AUTHORSHIP OF THE PENTATEUCH

SPECIAL TOPIC: LAWS IN THE ANE

▣ "in the ark" This depositing of special documents before the national god is characteristic of the ANE. Compare
Egyptian Book of the Dead (in a box under Thot's feet) and the Hittite Suzerain Treaties of the second millennium
B.C. See Introduction to the book,VII.

verses.zh: 于是我用皂荚木做了一柜，又凿出两块石版，和先前的一样，手里拿这两块版上山去了。
verses.en: So I made an ark of acacia[NOTE:1] wood and carved out two stone tablets just like the first ones. Then I went up the mountain with the two tablets in my hands.
notes: Acacia wood (Heb “shittim wood”). This is wood from the acacia, the most common timber tree of the Sinai region. Most likely it is the species Acacia raddiana because this has the largest trunk. See F. N. Hepper, Illustrated Encyclopedia of Bible Plants, 63.
verses.commentary:
10:3 "acacia wood" This was a hard, brownish-orange wood (BDB 1008) that grows in the desert. A member of the
mimosa family (see UBS Fauna and Flora of the Bible, pp.87-88). It was a common evergreen desert tree (cf. Isa. 41:19). This
wood is associated with all of the furniture of the tabernacle.

SPECIAL TOPIC: ACACIA WOOD

verses.zh: 耶和华将那大会之日、在山上从火中所传与你们的十条诫，照先前所写的，写在这版上，将版交给我了。
verses.en: The Lord[NOTE:1] then wrote on the tablets the same words,[NOTE:2] the Ten Commandments,[NOTE:3] which he[NOTE:4] had spoken to you at the mountain from the middle of the fire at the time of that assembly, and he[NOTE:5] gave them to me.
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (the Lord) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “according to the former writing.” See note on the phrase “the same words” in v. 2.
Heb “ten words.” The “Ten Commandments” are known in Hebrew as the “Ten Words,” which in Greek became the “Decalogue.”
Heb “the Lord.” The pronoun has been used in the translation for stylistic reasons to avoid redundancy.
Heb “the Lord.” See note on “he” earlier in this verse.
verses.commentary:
10:4 "the Ten Commandments" This is literally "the ten words" (BDB 796 CONSTRUCT BDB 182). These
basic characteristic, foundational laws are very brief and stated in general principles. They mandate an intimate, exclusive
relationship with YHWH (cf. Deut. 10:20), which is reflected in exclusive worship and obedience, which in turn mandates an
appropriate commiserate relationship with other covenant members (and also non-members, cf. Deut. 10:17-19). Knowing
YHWH impacts all of life and its priorities!

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE TEN COMMANDMENTS

▣ "on the mountain from the midst of the fire" This refers to YHWH's presence on Mt. Horeb/Sinai, recorded
in Exod. 19:16-20. His presence is described as a "consuming fire on the mountain" (cf. Exod. 24:17). This phrase if used
several times Deuteronomy (cf. Deut. 4:12,15,33,36; 5:4,24,26).

The fire (BDB 77) was imagery of YHWH's glorious presence:

- a torch in Gen. 15:17

- the burning bush in Exod. 3:2

- fire on Mt. Horeb, Exod. 19:18; Deut. 4:11,12,15,33,36

- the Shekinah pillar of fire in Exod. 13:21,22; 14:24; Num. 9:15,16; 14:14; Ps. 78:14 (see SPECIAL TOPIC: SHEKINAH)

- coals of fire in Ezekiel's vision of YHWH's portable throne chariot in Ezek. 1:13; 10:2

The Ten Commandments are repeatedly said to have been spoken from the midst of the fire
(cf. Deut. 4:12,15,33; 5:4,22,24,26; 9:10; 10:4). The commandments were personal, covenantal revelations from YHWH,
not the mind of Moses.

SPECIAL TOPIC: FIRE

verses.zh: 我转身下山，将这版放在我所做的柜中，现今还在那里，正如耶和华所吩咐我的。」
verses.en: Then I turned, went down the mountain, and placed the tablets into the ark I had made—they are still there, just as the Lord commanded me.

verses.zh: （以色列人从比罗比尼・亚干（或译：亚干井）起行，到了摩西拉。亚伦死在那里，就葬在那里。他儿子以利亚撒接续他供祭司的职分。
verses.en: During those days the Israelites traveled from Beeroth Bene Jaakan[NOTE:1] to Moserah.[NOTE:2] There Aaron died and was buried, and his son Eleazar became priest in his place.
notes: Beeroth Bene Jaakan. This Hebrew name could be translated “the wells of Bene Jaakan” or “the wells of the sons of Jaakan,” a site whose location cannot be determined (cf. Num 33:31-32; 1 Chr 1:42).
Moserah. Since Aaron in other texts (Num 20:28; 33:38) is said to have died on Mount Hor, this must be the Arabah region in which Hor was located.
verses.commentary:
10:6,7,9 SPECIAL TOPIC: LATER ADDITIONS TO DEUTERONOMY

10:6 "the sons of Israel" See SPECIAL TOPIC: ISRAEL (the name)

▣ "Beeroth Bene-jaakan to Moserah" The first two words (BDB 91,122) translate literally, "the wells of
the sons of Jaakan" (cf. Num. 33:31). Moserah means "chastisement" (BDB 64). Moserah (possibly a district), which may
be synonymous with Mt. Hor (cf. Num. 20:22-29; 33:38), is the place where Aaron died. These both refer to geographical
areas where the Israelites wandered.

▣ "Aaron died there" Numbers 20:27-28 says this happened at Mt. Hor. Aaron, like Moses, did not enter
the Promised Land because of his disobedience (cf. Num. 20:8,12).

▣ "Eleazar" His name means "God has helped" (BDB 46). He was the third son of Aaron (cf. Exod. 6:23). The
first two sons were killed because they took YHWH's commands lightly (cf. Lev. 10:1-7; Num. 3:4). The Rabbinical Midrash says
that because Lev. 10:9 restricts alcohol to priests while they are on duty that these two sons, Nadab and Abihu, were drunk.

The High Priesthood was to pass on through Aaron's family (cf. Exod. 29:9; 40:15; Num. 3:5-10; 25:13).

SPECIAL TOPIC: AARON'S SONS

SPECIAL TOPIC: LEVITICAL PRIESTS

verses.zh: 他们从那里起行，到了谷歌大，又从谷歌大到了有溪水之地的约巴他。
verses.en: From there they traveled to Gudgodah,[NOTE:1] and from Gudgodah to Jotbathah,[NOTE:2] a place of flowing streams.
notes: Gudgodah. This is probably the same as Haggidgad, which is also associated with Jotbathah (Num 33:33).

Jotbathah. This place, whose Hebrew name can be translated “place of wadis,” is possibly modern Ain Tabah, just north of Eilat, or Tabah, 6.5 mi (11 km) south of Eilat on the west shore of the Gulf of Aqaba.
verses.commentary:
10:7 "Gudgodah" The meaning of the name is uncertain (BDB 151). It is seemingly identified with Hor-haggidgad
in Num. 32:32. They are both places where Israel camped in her journey from Mt. Horeb/Sinai to Kadesh-barnea. The JPSOA
has "Gudgod."

▣ "Jotbathah" The word means "pleasantness" (BDB 406, probably because of the presence of water). It is
also mentioned as a campsite in Num. 33:33-34. The JPSOA has "Jotbath."

verses.zh: 那时，耶和华将利未支派分别出来，抬耶和华的约柜，又侍立在耶和华面前事奉他，奉他的名祝福，直到今日。
verses.en: At that time the Lord set apart the tribe of Levi[NOTE:1] to carry the ark of the Lord’s covenant, to stand before the Lord to serve him, and to formulate blessings[NOTE:2] in his name, as they do to this very day.
notes: The Lord set apart the tribe of Levi. This was not the initial commissioning of the tribe of Levi to this ministry (cf. Num 3:11-13; 8:12-26), but with Aaron’s death it seemed appropriate to Moses to reiterate Levi’s responsibilities. There is no reference in the Book of Numbers to this having been done, but the account of Eleazar’s succession to the priesthood there (Num 20:25-28) would provide a setting for this to have occurred.
To formulate blessings. The most famous example of this is the priestly “blessing formula” of Num 6:24-26.
verses.commentary:
10:8 "the Lord set apart the tribe of Levi" The VERB "set apart"
(BDB 95, KB 110, Hiphil PERFECT, cf. Num. 8:14; 16:9; 1 Chr. 23:13) means "to divide." Here the
separation is for

- special cultic service related to the tabernacle and later temple

- blessings of the people (cf. Deut. 10:8; Lev.9:22-23; Num. 6:22-27)

- judging the people's disputes (cf. Deut. 21:5)

- judging between clean and unclean (cf. Lev. 10:10)

This VERB is parallel to "choose" (BDB 103, KB 119, cf. Deut. 18:5; 21:5).

Israel was to be separate from the other nations (cf. Lev. 20:24-26; 1 Kgs. 8:53; i.e. "a holy nation,"
cf. Exod. 19:6), so the tribe of Levi was to be separated from the other tribes as YHWH's special cultic servants. They
were chosen because:

- Levi was from the tribe of Moses and Aaron

- the Levites took the place of the "first born" from Hebrew families (cf. Exod.13; Num. 3:12; 8:14-19)

- the Levites faithfully responded to Moses' call to punish Israel (cf. Exod. 32:25-29). In Gen. 29:34, Leah called
her third son Levi because her husband did not love her, but the child's name meant, "Jacob was attached
(or joined) to me" (BDB 532).

As the priestly tribe, some of them will

- carry the ark of the covenant

- stand before the Lord to serve Him (i.e. all the duties at the tabernacle and later, the temple, in Jerusalem, cf 18:5; Num. 18:1-7

- bless in His name (e.g. Num. 6:24-27)

Later there will develop specific tasks given to some families of Levi to be priests and others will
function as Levites. However, in Deuteronomy all Levites can act as priests (compare Deut. 31:9 and 25). See Roland deVaux,
Ancient Israel, vol. 2, pp. 358-371.

SPECIAL TOPIC: LEVITICAL PRIESTS

verses.zh: 所以利未人在他弟兄中无分无业，耶和华是他的产业，正如耶和华―你　神所应许他的。）
verses.en: Therefore Levi has no allotment or inheritance[NOTE:1] among his brothers;[NOTE:2] the Lord is his inheritance just as the Lord your God told him.
notes: Levi has no allotment or inheritance. As the priestly tribe, Levi would have no land allotment except for forty-eight towns set apart for their use (Num 35:1-8; Josh 21:1-42). But theirs was a far greater inheritance, for the Lord himself was their apportionment, that is, service to him would be their full-time and lifelong privilege (Num 18:20-24; Deut 18:2; Josh 13:33).
That is, among the other Israelite tribes.
verses.commentary:
10:9 "Levi does not have a portion or inheritance" The tribe of Levi was not given any land allotment, however, parts
of forty-eight cities were given to them with their surrounding pasture land (cf. Num. 35:1-8; Joshua 21).

▣ "the Lord is his inheritance" This denoted their special place of
service (cf. Num. 18:20; Deut. 10:9; 18:1,2; Josh. 13:33; Ezek. 44:28)! This wonderful promise to the tribe of Levi became a
cry from the heart of every true believer (cf. Ps. 16:5; 73:23-28; 119:57; 142:5; Lam. 3:24).

SPECIAL TOPIC: BELIEVERS' INHERITANCE

verses.zh: 「我又像从前在山上住了四十昼夜。那次耶和华也应允我，不忍将你灭绝。
verses.en: As for me, I stayed at the mountain as I did the first time, 40 days and nights. The Lord listened to me that time as well and decided not to destroy you.
verses.commentary:
10:10 "forty nights like the first time" See Exod. 34:28; Deut. 9:18.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SYMBOLIC NUMBERS IN SCRIPTURE, #7

▣ "the Lord was not willing to destroy you" This was Moses' intercessory ministry (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: INTERCESSORY PRAYER, cf. Deut. 9:25-29;
Exod. 32:9-14).

verses.zh: 耶和华吩咐我说：『你起来引导这百姓，使他们进去得我向他们列祖起誓应许所赐之地。』」
verses.en: Then he[NOTE:1] said to me, “Get up, set out leading[NOTE:2] the people so they may go and possess[NOTE:3] the land I promised to give to their ancestors.”[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “the Lord.” See note on “he” in 10:4.
Heb “before” (so KJV, ASV); NAB, NRSV “at the head of.”
After the imperative these subordinated jussive forms (with prefixed vav) indicate purpose or result.
Heb “fathers” (also in vv. 15, 22).
verses.commentary:
10:11 YHWH commanded Israel to act on what He had already promised-the conquest of the Promised Land:

- "arise" ‒ BDB 877, KB 1086, Qal IMPERATIVE SINGULAR, cf. Deut. 2:13,24, which are
PLURAL and refer to Israel. Here the SINGULAR refers to Moses.

- "proceed" ‒ BDB 229, KB 246, Qal IMPERATIVE SINGULAR, literally means "break camp
and start the next stage of the journey" (cf. Exod. 17:1; 40:36,38;l Num. 10:2,12; 33:1,2). Moses was to lead the people onward.

- "they may go in" ‒ BDB 97, KB 112, Qal IMPERATIVE PLURAL, which may be functioning as a
JUSSIVE

- "and possess the land" ‒ BDB 439, KB 441, Qal IMPERFECT PLURAL, which may be functioning as a
JUSSIVE (see SPECIAL
TOPIC: POSSESS THE LAND)

Israel is called on to fulfill YHWH's oath to the Patriarchs (cf. Deut. 1:8; Josh. 21:43). God uses human
instrumentality (e.g. Exod. 3:7-12)! It is His power and purpose, but His covenant people must act in faith and trust!

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT PROMISES TO THE PATRIARCHS

verses.zh: 「以色列啊，现在耶和华―你　神向你所要的是甚么呢？只要你敬畏耶和华―你的　神，遵行他的道，爱他，尽心尽性事奉他，
verses.en: Now, Israel, what does the Lord your God require of you except to revere him,[NOTE:1] to obey all his commandments,[NOTE:2] to love him, to serve him[NOTE:3] with all your mind and being,[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “the Lord your God.” See note on “he” in 10:4.
Heb “to walk in all his ways” (so KJV, NIV84, NRSV); NIV11 “walk in obedience to him”; NAB “follow his ways exactly”; NLT “to live according to his will.”
Heb “the Lord your God.” See note on “he” in 10:4.
Heb “heart and soul” or “heart and being”; NCV “with your whole being.” See note on the word “being” in Deut 6:5.
verses.commentary:
10:12-13 See the following three Special Topics.

- SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S COVENANT REQUIREMENTS OF ISRAEL

- SPECIAL TOPIC: FEAR (OT)

- SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP

verses.zh: 遵守他的诫命律例，就是我今日所吩咐你的，为要叫你得福。
verses.en: and to keep the Lord’s commandments and statutes that I am giving[NOTE:1] you today for your own good?
notes: Heb “commanding” (so NASB, NRSV). For stylistic reasons, to avoid redundancy, “giving” has been used in the translation.
verses.commentary: 10:13 "for your good" Obedience brings blessing; disobedience brings judgment (cf. Deuteronomy 27-29; Leviticus 26).

verses.zh: 看哪，天和天上的天，地和地上所有的，都属耶和华―你的　神。
verses.en: The heavens—indeed the highest heavens—belong to the Lord your God, as does the earth and everything in it.
verses.commentary:
10:14 This verse implies monotheism. This refers to the atmosphere of this planet, the universe (starry canopy), and
the throne of God (i.e. the three heavens).

SPECIAL TOPIC: MONOTHEISM

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE HEAVENS AND THE THIRD HEAVEN

verses.zh: 耶和华但喜悦你的列祖，爱他们，从万民中拣选他们的后裔，就是你们，像今日一样。
verses.en: However, only to your ancestors did he[NOTE:1] show his loving favor,[NOTE:2] and he chose you, their descendants,[NOTE:3] from all peoples—as is apparent today.
notes: Heb “the Lord.” See note on “he” in 10:4.

Heb “take delight to love.” Here again the verb אָהֵב (ʾahev, “love”), juxtaposed with בָחַר (bakhar, “choose”), is a term in covenant contexts that describes the Lord’s initiative in calling the patriarchal ancestors to be the founders of a people special to him (cf. the note on the word “loved” in Deut 4:37).
The Hebrew text includes “after them,” but it is redundant in English style and has not been included in the translation.
verses.commentary:
10:15 Notice the parallel ways of describing YHWH's election of Israel as His special people (i.e. "even
you above all peoples," cf. Exod. 19:5-6; Deut. 7:6; 14:2):

- "set His affection" ‒ BDB 365 I, KB 362, Qal PERFECT, cf. Deut. 7:7. In Deut. 4:37 the
other word for love (BDB 12, KB 17) is used.

- "He chose their descendants" ‒ BDB 103, KB 119, Qal IMPERFECT with waw, cf. Deut. 4:37.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HE CHOSE US

▣ "as it is this day" This may be a textual marker of a later editor. Notice "until this day" in v. 11.
See note at Deut. 3:14.

verses.zh: 所以你们要将心里的污秽除掉，不可再硬着颈项。
verses.en: Therefore, cleanse[NOTE:1] your hearts and stop being so stubborn![NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “circumcise the foreskin of” (cf. KJV, ASV, NRSV). Reference to the Abrahamic covenant prompts Moses to recall the sign of that covenant, namely, physical circumcision (Gen 17:9-14). Just as that act signified total covenant obedience, so spiritual circumcision (cleansing of the heart) signifies more internally a commitment to be pliable and obedient to the will of God (cf. Deut 30:6; Jer 4:4; 9:26).
Heb “your neck do not harden again.” See note on the word “stubborn” in Deut 9:6.
verses.commentary:
10:16 Israel was to respond to YHWH's choice by:

- "circumcise your heart" ‒ BDB 557, KB 555, Qal PERFECT with waw. This is imagery
of openness to God (cf. Lev. 26:41; Deut. 10:16; 30:6; Jer. 4:4; 9:25-26). It is expressed in several ways:

- circumcise your flesh ‒ Gen. 17:14 (covenant sign)

- circumcise your lips ‒ idiom in Exod. 6:12,30

- circumcise your ears ‒ Jer. 6:10

- refers to a true heart, not just body circumcision ‒ Deut. 30:6; Jer. 4:4; 9:25-26; Ezek. 44:9; Rom. 2:28-29

- "stiffen your neck no more" ‒ BDB 904, KB 1151, Hiphil IMPERFECT,
cf. Deut. 9:6,7,13,24,27; 31:27. See note at Deut. 2:30.

SPECIAL TOPIC: CIRCUMCISION

SPECIAL TOPIC: STUBBORNNESS (OT)

verses.zh: 因为耶和华―你们的　神―他是万神之神，万主之主，至大的　神，大有能力，大而可畏，不以貌取人，也不受贿赂。
verses.en: For the Lord your God is God of gods and Lord of lords, the great, mighty, and awesome God who is unbiased and takes no bribe,
verses.commentary:
10:17 Notice the accolades used to describe YHWH:

- God of gods ‒ BDB 43, cf. Ps. 136:2

- Lord of lords ‒ BDB 10, cf. Ps. 136:3

- the great God ‒ BDB 152, cf. Deut. 3:24; 5:24; 9:26; 11:2; 32:3; Neh. 1:5; 9:32

- the mighty God ‒ BDB 150, cf. Neh. 9:32; Ps. 24:8; Isa. 10:21

- the awesome God ‒ BDB 431, KB 432, Niphal PARTICIPLE, cf. Deut. 7:21; Neh. 1:5; 9:32

Several of these titles come from the titles of pagan gods which Israel began to use for YHWH. Listing of
several descriptive titles for deity is common in the ANE. In the Babylonian Creation Account (i.e. Enuma Elish), Marduk is
given 50 different, magnificient titles.

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHARACTERISTICS OF ISRAEL'S GOD (NT)

▣ "who does not show partiality" The Hebrew phrase means "who does not lift up faces" (BDB 669,
KB 724, Qal IMPERFECT plus BDB 815). This is used often of judges (cf. Deut. 1:17; 16:19; 24:17;
Lev. 19:15). This implies that YHWH is a God of fair judgment (cf. Deut. 10:17; 2 Chr. 19:7).

▣ "nor take a bribe" YHWH's character is described in human legal terms (cf. Deut. 10:18-19). This is often
associated with the above phrase. YHWH does not need anything from humans. He cannot be bribed or manipulated.

verses.zh: 他为孤儿寡妇伸冤，又怜爱寄居的，赐给他衣食。
verses.en: who justly treats[NOTE:1] the orphan and widow, and who loves resident foreigners, giving them food and clothing.
notes: Or “who executes justice for” (so NAB, NRSV); NLT “gives justice to.” Cf. Exod 22:21; Lev 19:33-34; Deut 24:14, 17; 27:19.
verses.commentary:
10:18-19 Notice how the legal characteristics of YHWH in Deut. 10:18 are put into practice:

- "He executes (BDB 793 I, KB 889, Qal PARTICIPLE) justice for":

- the orphan

- the widow (cf. Deut. 24:17; 26:12-13; 27:19; Ps. 68:4-5)

- "shows His love (BDB 12, KB 17, Qal PARTICIPLE) for the alien by giving him"
(BDB 678, KB 733, Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT):

- food

- clothing

The Israelites are to do these things for two reasons:

- It reflects the character of their God (Deut. 10:17; Isa. 58:6-7,10; see SPECIAL TOPIC: CHARACTERISTICS OF ISRAEL'S GOD [OT]).

- They know how being treated unfairly feels (Deut. 10:19; 24:18,22; Exod. 22:21; 23:9).

Exodus 22:22-23 also mentions that YHWH will hear the prayers of these socially powerless ones
and act on their behalf (cf. Ps. 146:9; Mal. 3:5; as will the Messiah, cf. Isa. 11:4). This is what the human kings of the ANE were
expected to do, but in reality, they catered to the rich and powerful.

verses.zh: 所以你们要怜爱寄居的，因为你们在埃及地也作过寄居的。
verses.en: So you must love the resident foreigner because you were foreigners in the land of Egypt.

verses.zh: 你要敬畏耶和华―你的　神，事奉他，专靠他，也要指着他的名起誓。
verses.en: Revere the Lord your God, serve him, be loyal to him, and take oaths only in his name.
verses.commentary:
10:20 As the requirements of YHWH were set out in Deut. 10:12-13 by several INFINITIVE CONSTRUCTS, here
they are set our again in Qal IMPERFECT VERBS:

- "fear the Lord" ‒ BDB 431, KB 432, cf. Deut. 5:29; 6:13; 13:4 (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: FEAR (OT)

- "serve Him" ‒ BDB 712, KB 773, cf. Deut. 13:4

- "cling to Him" ‒ BDB 179, KB 209, cf. Deut. 11:22; 13:4

- "swear by His name" ‒ BDB 989, KB 1396, cf. Deut. 5:11; 6:13. See full note at Deut. 5:11 (see SPECIAL TOPIC: CALL ON THE NAME).

All of these relate to proper motives and actions of worship (see SPECIAL TOPIC: WORSHIP).

verses.zh: 他是你所赞美的，是你的　神，为你做了那大而可畏的事，是你亲眼所看见的。
verses.en: He is the one you should praise;[NOTE:1] he is your God, the one who has done these great and awesome things for you that you have seen.
notes: Heb “your praise.” The pronoun is subjective and the noun “praise” is used here metonymically for the object of their praise (the Lord).
verses.commentary:
10:21 "He is your praise" The language of Deuteronomy has much in common with Wisdom Literature (see
SPECIAL TOPIC: WISDOM LITERATURE). This
phrase is seen in Ps. 109:1. There is no VERB with this phrase or the next one. They are strong
affirmations that YHWH's redemptive action during the exodus and wilderness wandering period are praiseworthy:

- their praise (BDB 239)

- their Elohim (BDB 43; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, C.)

▣ "who has done these great and awesome things for you which you have seen" This refers to YHWH's
actions and provisions during the exodus from Egypt, the wilderness wandering period (cf. Deut. 11:2), and that which
will be repeated during the conquest!

verses.zh: 你的列祖七十人下埃及；现在耶和华―你的　神使你如同天上的星那样多。」
verses.en: When your ancestors went down to Egypt, they numbered only seventy, but now the Lord your God has made you as numerous as the stars of the sky.[NOTE:1]
notes: Or “heavens.” The Hebrew term שָׁמַיִם (shamayim) may be translated “heaven(s)” or “sky” depending on the context.
verses.commentary:
10:22 "seventy persons in all" Seventy is a round number used of people. See Genesis 46:27; Exod. 1:5.

One text of Exod. 1:5, found at Qumran (i.e. Dead Sea Scrolls) has the number 75, which matches
Acts 7:14-15. For a good brief discussion of the different numbers, see Hard Sayings of the Bible, p. 521 or
Gleason L. Archer, Encyclopedia of Bible Difficulties, pp. 378-379.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SYMBOLIC NUMBERS IN SCRIPTURE, #8

▣ "as the stars of heaven" This is a fulfillment of YHWH's promise to Abraham. See full notes at Gen. 13:16 and Deut. 1:10.
